solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Governor's weakness regarding young woman

definitions.note: an adjective: belonging to a viceroy, a governor ruling for a monarch

parts.note: a vice is a moral weakness or failing
re means regarding, as in a letter heading
gal is an informal word for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Someone describes a governor's particular failing as an interest in a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Viceregal describes a viceroy, a colonial ruler governing on the sovereign's behalf, so it is the possessive 'Governor's' in adjective form.

clue.text: Bigshot meeting the queen is traitor

parts.note: a VIP, very important person, is a bigshot
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A dignitary granted an audience with the monarch turns out to be a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A viper, a venomous snake, is figuratively a treacherous person who turns on those who trust them.

clue.text: Ideal location to film, perhaps, with soft light

parts.note: to film over is one way to cloud, as an eye or a glass clouds
soft in the head, crazy, is cuckoo
to light on something is to land on it, as a bird alights

explanation.surface: A cinematographer picks the perfect place to shoot in gentle lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to film' looks like movie-making; it is the verb meaning to become hazy, and 'soft' and 'light' are both verbs or adjectives in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloud-cuckoo-land is a dreamer's imaginary utopia, an idealised place unconnected with reality.

clue.text: Appear again, as army corps heading north to meet another southbound

parts.note: a second army corps, RE (Royal Engineers), read in the normal top-to-bottom direction

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means the letters read upward, so this pair is turned round

parts.note: eg, for example, can stand for as, as in 'animals such as...'
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops are seen again as one column marches north to meet another marching south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' reverses the two pieces before it, since in a down entry northward means read upward, giving EMERGE. 'as' looks like a link word but gives letters (as = for example).
explanation.definitionFit: To re-emerge is to come out into view once more, to reappear.

clue.text: Setter welcoming public turning up old source of common heritage?

indicators.note: welcoming means taking guests in, so the setting agent holds the rest inside it

parts.note: a gel is something that sets, a setting agent

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means read upward, so the word for public is reversed

parts.note: open means public, available to all

explanation.surface: A crossword setter makes a public appearance, revealing an ancient source of shared ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is not the crossword compiler but a substance that sets; 'turning up' gives NEPO, which goes inside with O.
explanation.definitionFit: A gene pool is the stock of genes in a population, from which its members inherit their shared traits.

clue.text: Watch as diver secures approval

indicators.note: secures means holds fast, so the bird's name grips the approval inside it

parts.note: the loon is a diving bird, called a diver in Britain
OK is an expression of approval

explanation.surface: Spectators watch while a diver wins the judges' approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diver' suggests a swimmer, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To look on is to watch as a spectator without taking part.

clue.text: On vacation, Ronnie Barker's to make comeback

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, so the name keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: a cur is a dog, a barker

explanation.surface: The comedian Ronnie Barker plans a return to the stage after a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronnie Barker was a much-loved British TV comedian; here 'Barker' is just a dog. 'On vacation' empties RONNIE to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen again, to come back after an absence.

clue.text: Sale to make good Eeyore's loss?

definitions.meaning: the sale of goods to the public
Eeyore, the donkey in Winnie-the-Pooh, loses his tail

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's sale seems meant to make up for Eeyore's misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: In Winnie-the-Pooh the donkey Eeyore loses his tail and Pooh finds it, so the second reading splits the answer into RE- and TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail is selling goods in small quantities to consumers, and as a verb to sell; pinning a tail back on is to re-tail.

clue.text: Money-making run in snooker that won't air on BBC

definitions.meaning: a break is a scoring run in snooker, and a commercial one would be one that earns money
the BBC carries no advertising, so it never shows a pause for adverts

explanation.surface: A snooker player's lucrative break would never be shown on the publicly funded BBC.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC is Britain's licence-fee-funded broadcaster, which carries no adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial break is the interval in a programme for advertisements, which the advert-free BBC never has.

clue.text: Artist to overhaul image — time to grasp medium

indicators.note: to grasp means to hold within, so the word for overhauling an image holds the letter for medium

parts.note: to rebrand is to give a product or company a new image
M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: An artist needs to refresh his image, and it is time he grasped a new medium.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt was the great seventeenth-century Dutch painter, the archetypal Old Master.

clue.text: Tripe on toast is source of this

definitions.text: Tripe on toast is source of this

indicators.note: toast here means ruined, done for, so the letters are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A snack of tripe on toast provides plenty of a certain nutrient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toast' looks like the bread; as in 'you're toast', it means destroyed, the anagram signal. The whole clue is also true: the dish supplies this nutrient.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is offal, rich in protein, the nutrient found in meat that builds body tissue.

clue.text: Oscar training a single parent to become model?

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
PT, physical training, is exercise
I is the Roman numeral one
mum is a mother, a parent

explanation.surface: Oscar's fitness regime turns a single mother into a model.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the best possible, an ideal case, much as a model is a perfect example to copy.

clue.text: Slope that's good for breaking in horse

indicators.note: breaking in means entering by force, so the letter for good is inserted into the riding word

parts.note: to horse is to provide with or ride a horse, so the verb here is ride

explanation.surface: A trainer chooses a hillside that suits breaking in a young horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking in' is a horsy phrase for training an animal; here it signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long raised strip of land whose sides slope away, so it can stand for a slope.

clue.text: Member of upper house maintaining backing for appeal gets cash in

definitions.note: a verb phrase; to profiteer is to cash in, making excessive profit

indicators.note: maintaining means holding up or keeping within, so the lord holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a peer sits in the House of Lords, Britain's upper house

indicators.note: backing means turned back, so the word for is read in reverse

parts.note: it is a dated word for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A lord with an interest in a charity appeal is accused of lining his pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' gives ROF; 'it' for sex appeal is a dated usage, as in Clara Bow, the 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: To profiteer is to exploit a shortage or crisis to make an unfair profit, cashing in on others' need.

clue.text: Club to move against being infiltrated by left

indicators.note: being infiltrated means having something get inside, so the letter for left goes into the moving word

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly
on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall

explanation.surface: A political club is urged to make a move against left-wing infiltrators.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a heavy stick or cudgel used as a weapon, which is a kind of club.

clue.text: Knees apart, prayed for someone wise to intercede

indicators.note: to intercede is to step in between, so the bird goes inside the pleading word

parts.note: to beg for is to pray for, plead
the owl is proverbially wise

explanation.surface: Someone kneeling in prayer begs a wise figure to intervene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knees apart' looks like a posture for praying; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bow-legged has legs curving outwards, so the knees stay apart when the feet are together.

clue.text: Search for cat, perhaps, when case is raised?

definitions.meaning: to search an area or text quickly

definitions.text: for cat, perhaps, when case is raised?
definitions.meaning: written in upper case, cat becomes CAT

explanation.surface: A search for a lost cat happens whenever the case of a missing pet is raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is not a matter under investigation but letter case: upper-case CAT is computerised axial tomography, a kind of scan.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to look over something carefully; a CAT scan is a medical imaging scan.

clue.text: Who, in French, takes online exam, perhaps most subdued in conversation?

indicators.note: takes means picks up something extra, so the French word is followed by the exam

parts.note: qui is French for who
an e-test would be an electronic, online test

explanation.surface: A French speaker sitting an online exam is the least talkative of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: The quietest person is the most restrained and least loud, the most subdued when talking.

clue.text: Pets going head to head inside very well broken up

indicators.note: inside means within, so the facing pets sit between the letters for very well

parts.note: so can mean very well, as in agreeing 'so be it', or so as very
two cats nose to nose: one reads backwards (TAC) and meets the other (CAT)

explanation.surface: Two pets squaring up indoors leave everything thoroughly broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head to head' means one CAT is written backwards so their heads meet in the middle: TAC + CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato describes notes played detached from each other, so the music is broken up rather than smooth.

clue.text: Turned on the new PC?

definitions.meaning: the past of wake, to stir into life, and also means alert or switched on
being ... is seen as the current version of political correctness

explanation.surface: Someone switched on a freshly bought personal computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' looks like a personal computer; it is political correctness.
explanation.definitionFit: Woke means alert to social injustice, often equated with political correctness; it is also the past tense of wake.

clue.text: Take away inferior piece of land?

parts.note: sub means below or inferior, as in substandard
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to remove a poor-quality plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to deduct one quantity from another, to take it away.

clue.text: After extremes of pace, pole positions altered in race

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the rearranged pole follows the ends of pace
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
positions altered means the letters swap places, an anagram

explanation.surface: In a motor race the pole positions are reshuffled after a change of pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pole positions' looks like motor racing; 'pole' is the fodder and 'positions altered' the anagram signal, giving OPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A people is a nation or ethnic group, which is one sense of race.

clue.text: Mother and one close to her in family tree

parts.note: a dam is a mother, especially of an animal

parts.words: one close to her in family
parts.note: a son is a close family member of his mother

explanation.surface: A mother and her nearest relative appear together on the family tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family tree' looks like a phrase; 'tree' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The damson is a small plum tree bearing dark purple fruit.

clue.text: No longer blame former lover I esteem

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
I is the Roman numeral for one
to rate is to esteem, think highly of

explanation.surface: Someone forgives a former partner, saying they still hold them in high regard.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear someone of an accusation, so they are no longer held responsible.

clue.text: Solid copper pen manufacturer

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Bic is a maker of ballpoint pens

explanation.surface: A sturdy copper pen comes from a well-known manufacturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solid' reads as an adjective for the pen, but it is the definition, as in a solid shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubic describes a three-dimensional shape, a solid, or a measure of volume.

clue.text: Key underpinning native American belief system

indicators.note: underpinning means supporting from below, so in this down entry the musical key goes underneath

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
D is a musical key

explanation.surface: A key tenet supports the beliefs of a Native American people.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of religious beliefs or guiding principles, a system of belief.

clue.text: Heavy breather coming round to eat spread

indicators.note: coming round means turning about, so the two words are read backwards together

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper or drink
marg is short for margarine, a spread

explanation.surface: A noisy breather wakes up just in time to eat breakfast with a bread spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming round' sounds like waking from unconsciousness; it reverses SUPMARG.
explanation.definitionFit: A grampus is a dolphin-like sea creature famed for loud blowing, so a person who breathes heavily is called one.

clue.text: Poet's before entry to West Stand

indicators.note: in an across entry going west means right to left, so these words are reversed

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
a gate is an entrance, a way of entry

explanation.surface: A poet arrives before the gate into a stand on the West side of a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Stand' looks like part of a sports ground; 'to West' reverses ERE + GATE to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An étagère is a piece of furniture with open shelves, a stand for displaying ornaments.

clue.text: Regularly goes by Pentagon stratagem

indicators.note: by means next to, so the alternate letters sit beside the department

parts.note: the Pentagon houses the DoD, the US Department of Defense

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is picked

explanation.surface: The Pentagon routinely relies on a clever ploy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a cunning trick or evasive scheme, the same as a stratagem.

clue.text: Made useful contacts — indicating trawl was successful?

definitions.meaning: to network is to build useful professional relationships
the fishing net did its job

explanation.surface: A fisherman's good haul shows that making contacts paid off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into NET and WORKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who networked cultivated connections with people who could help their career.
